genre_name: Single-cell atlas analysis of cell states and drug sensitivity
scope: Original research papers that build or reuse a single-cell (scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, CITE-seq, multiome; often with spatial data) atlas, define cell types and states (clustering, markers, programmes, trajectories, CNV-inferred malignant cells, cell-cell communication), then link states to drug sensitivity, therapy response or druggable targets (drug2cell, DREEP-style GDSC/CTRP/PRISM projection, ex vivo drug data, immunotherapy-response cohorts), usually validated in bulk cohorts (survival, deconvolution), cell-line data, spatial data or wet-lab experiments. Covers both atlas-of-public-data papers and papers adding new samples. Excludes pure method or benchmark papers for single-cell tools, perturbation-screen technology papers, reviews and database or resource-only papers.

limitations.placement: No fixed home. Explicit limitations text in 3/9: a 'Limitations of the study' subsection closing the Discussion (1/9, Cell Reports Medicine) or an unheaded Discussion paragraph opening 'Our study has (several) limitations' (2/9). 5/9 scatter caveat sentences through the Discussion, often in the last paragraph; 1/9 (Nature) states none.
conventions: When present, one paragraph of 115-210 words inside or closing the Discussion, items introduced as 'First, ... Second, ...'.
Cell Press papers should carry a 'Limitations of the study' heading (1 of 3 Cell Press exemplars does).
Closes by pointing to the needed validation (prospective cohorts, functional experiments).
Nature-family papers rarely have a limitations paragraph (0/4 explicit).

standard_items.text: State-response links are computational or associational; functional experiments or prospective cohorts are needed before any clinical use.
Technical limits of the assay: dropout, under-capture of low-mRNA cells (e.g. neutrophils), nuclear vs whole-cell RNA, fusion transcripts not detectable.
Single-region or single-time-point sampling and few samples per patient cannot capture intratumour heterogeneity.
Clinical, genotype or treatment metadata in public datasets are sparse or inconsistent, limiting subgroup analyses.
Association of a state with response does not show that the state causes it; co-varying cell types (e.g. fibroblasts) may drive it.
Therapy-response or outcome cohorts are small, retrospective or use an imperfect comparator (e.g. PD-L1 by transcript).
Drug-response knowledge from cell lines or pharmacogenomic screens may not transfer to patient tumours.

variation_notes: House style drives most structural variation. Cell Press (E1, E5, E6): 'Summary' abstract of about 150 words plus Highlights, In brief and graphical abstract; STAR Methods with Key Resources Table and Resource availability (data and code statements live there); 'Limitations of the study' expected but present in 1/3. Nature family (E2, E3, E7, E9): unheaded lead paragraphs in Nature and Nature Cancer, Results without a heading in Nature, Methods after Discussion, separate Data availability and Code availability, Reporting Summary (3/4), Extended Data figures (8-12) and source data. Genome Biology (E4): structured abstract, 'Background', a separate Conclusions section, Methods last, Declarations block, review history. eLife (E8): Materials and methods last, figure supplements, MDAR checklist, eLife assessment and public reviews appended. Design variation: 7/9 add new single-cell data and 8/9 run some wet-lab work; only E5 and E9 rest on public single-cell data alone (E9 entirely computational). The drug link ranges from drug-target scoring per state (drug2cell, DREEP, ex vivo LC50; 3/9) to immunotherapy-response association through bulk signatures (3/9) to clinical TKI response (1/9) and experimental targeting (1/9); E4 links states only to prognosis.
lint_notes: Canonical order is Methods-last (introduction, results, discussion, methods; 9/9). Do not fail a Methods-last draft for missing IMRaD order.
Results must be split into 5-11 headed subsections; the first should present the atlas with numbers (cells, samples or patients, datasets, platforms).

Every reused dataset needs an accession or source (GSE, E-MTAB, EGA, PRJNA, Synapse, TCGA, CELLxGENE) in the data statement, Key Resources Table or dataset table; the integrated object must have a named deposit (Zenodo, figshare, CELLxGENE or a portal).
Code availability needs a repository URL (GitHub or OSF); recommend a Zenodo DOI (3/9 do).
UMAP captions should state what colour encodes (cell type, state, dataset) and the number of cells; at least one embedding must be in the main text.
A drug-sensitivity figure must name the drug resource (ChEMBL, GDSC, CTRP, PRISM, CMap or an ex vivo screen) and the scoring method in its caption or in Methods; a drug claim without one fails.
Comparisons across conditions should be patient-level or pseudobulk (7/9); flag per-cell p-values used for between-patient claims.
Multiple-testing correction is stated in 9/9; require it whenever DE or association tests are reported.
When malignant and non-malignant cells are separated, require a CNV-inference method (inferCNV, CopyKAT, Numbat, SCEVAN; 4/9).
Integration-quality metrics (LISI, kBET, scIB) appear in 0/9 exemplars. Recommend them but do not fail drafts that lack them.
Ethics statement is conditional: required with new human material (6/6), absent in public-data papers (0/3). Amani's fixed public-data line is acceptable.
A KM plot must report n per group and a log-rank p or hazard ratio; the paper writer's figure table has no KM kind, so add one.

Venue add-ons: Cell Press needs Highlights, In brief, graphical abstract, STAR Methods with Key Resources Table and 'Limitations of the study'; Nature family needs separate Data and Code availability and a Reporting Summary.

No exemplar has a cell-filtering flow diagram; Amani's data-flow diagram (raw cells, then QC-filtered cells, then annotated cells per dataset) goes beyond the genre and fits the supplement or Figure 1.
notes: Share with new wet-lab data or experimental validation: 7/9 generated new single-cell data (all but E5 and E9); 8/9 report some wet-lab work (E5 only NK-92 coculture assays in Methods); 7/9 show wet-lab panels in main figures; 1/9 (E9) is entirely computational on public data. Amani's public-data-only papers will sit at the computational end of the genre, so the missing experimental arm must be stated as a limitation.
New display-item ids not in the shared vocabulary: bulk_cohort_projection, spatial_map.
E6 was measured from the PMC author manuscript (NIHMS1978911); the published version may differ slightly in word counts.
Nature-family 'web summary' and the eLife assessment are journal-written and are not author sections.
E4 (Genome Biology) links states to prognosis and immunotherapy resistance only in the text; it was kept as the BMC/OA computational-venue exemplar with that caveat.
Body-text mentions of 'pancreatic' (E1, E6, E9) are dataset lists or an adverse-event term; title, abstract and keywords of all 9 exemplars are clean (contamination_title_abstract empty).

PMC pages were blocked by a reCAPTCHA after one request; supplement contents for E2, E3, E7, E9 come from the publisher pages, for E1, E5, E8 from PMC XML captions, for E4 from one PMC page, and for E6 from in-text references to Tables S1-S10 (descriptions inferred).
Figure-kind tallies come from keyword screens of full captions plus spot reading. Composite multi-panel figures were scored per panel kind, so one figure can count for several kinds.
Limitation-theme frequencies come from a regex screen of Discussion text plus reading the three explicit limitations paragraphs. They are approximate.

Amani-relevant limitations no exemplar names explicitly (fewer than 2): batch or over-correction artefacts from integrating many datasets (only hinted in E1), and bulk-deconvolution confounding by stromal content (1/9, E4). Amani's writer should still include them when they apply.
